title: Inquest set in death of man held by police
article: A coroner's inquest will be held to determine how and why a 22-year-old Houston man was shot to death while in RCMP custody last month.

Coroner Shane DeMeyer said Thursday in a news release that the inquest into the shooting death of Ian Geoffrey Bush will be launched once separate investigations by both the B.C. Coroner's Service and the RCMP have concluded.

According to DeMeyer, the inquest will allow for the public presentation of all evidence relating to Bush's death. The coroner and a five-person jury will hear evidence from subpoenaed witnesses in order to determine the facts surrounding the death. The jury will then have an opportunity to make recommendations aimed at preventing future deaths from occurring under similar circumstances, as well as other relevant recommendations.
The date and location of the inquest have yet to be determined.

Bush died Oct. 29 of a single gunshot wound to the head, an initial autopsy determined. A more detailed autopsy report is still underway and could take up to six weeks to complete, the coroner's service said.
Police said Bush had been arrested earlier in the evening on a charge of obstructing a police officer.
Before his arrest, Bush had been at a hockey game with friends at the local area.

RCMP Corp. Tom Seaman said police came into contact with Bush between game periods outside the arena, where he was allegedly caught holding a beer. Seaman said police poured the beer out, but took Bush into custody after he refused to tell police his real name.

Approximately one hour later, Bush was dead. Police said he became violent after being released from jail and attacked an officer. No further details on what happened have been forthcoming from the RCMP.
Seaman said Thursday the police investigation is continuing, describing it as "a priority."
The officer involved -- a junior RCMP member with less than five years experience -- has since been put on paid administrative leave pending the investigation, Seaman said.
Seaman said the officer is also still recovering from injuries suffered during the altercation. He was treated in hospital after the incident, but has since been released, Seaman added.

Investigators from the Lower Mainland's specialized Integrated Homicide Investigation Team and major crime units have been dispatched to the northern RCMP detachment to aid in the internal investigation. The investigation is being headed up by officers from surrounding RCMP detachments.
Seaman called the shooting "a tragic event for everyone involved - - number one, for the Bush family, \[but also for\] our members and the community itself."
Houston is a town of 4,300 people, located between Prince Rupert and Prince George on Highway 16.
